correctness.rationale: For k>0 the gap bijection has A>=s+t and exactly s+t inactive gaps. A one in active gap i contributes C(i,s)C(A−i,t), as positions of the selected zeroes before and after it are independent. Setting u=A−s−t+1 and j=i−s gives weight at least (j+1)(u−j)=u+j(u−1−j), so u*h<=k for h active ones. The inequality u+h<=uh+1 gives M<=s+t+k, and enumeration of the inactive gaps yields the stated fixed-k length series. For n>=k+1 a term with n<M has 0<=n−M+d<d and vanishes in both interpretations. At n=k only maximal M contributes a defect of (−1)^d per configuration. Equality requires uh=k and u=1 or h=1. The u=1 configuration always exists; when h=1 and k>=2 an interior gap has weight>k, and the two endpoints contribute exactly for t=1 and s=1 respectively. When k=1 these cases coincide. The u=1 term also makes the leading coefficient strictly positive. Inspected check.py and its recorded output, not executed. Independently enumerated literal position tuples for n=0..10, s,t=1..3, k=1..6, and counted active vectors via multisets: 594 length identities and 54 exact signed-defect checks passed. Replay: python3 /workspace/check_three_run_independent.py. The unbounded conclusion rests on the inequalities and equality classification, not those checks.

evidence: The Bruda proof explicitly writes an eventual sum of binomial polynomials and derives the degree from the maximum number of long runs; its subsequent singleton-run construction gives lower-bound families. The gap bound u*h<=k and the equality conditions u+h=k+1 and w=k for h=1 give both a matching upper-support bound and the exact multiplicity at the upper support. Those complementary restrictions are absent from the general degree proof.

value.rationale: A natural infinite pattern family admits a stabilization age bounded solely by the frequency, even for arbitrarily long outer runs. The exact nonzero defect shows this bound is attained for each parameter choice and identifies precisely when additional maximal configurations occur. Those facts refine prior eventual polynomiality substantively; the degree statement by itself would not.
